body:
Cold highlight navigation and automatic device resume could land one spread early. Typography was applied in the late rendered callback after the paginator measured its target. In addition, later EPUB resize formatting replaced manually assigned logical padding with its own gutter-derived physical padding; desktop defaults could hide the defect while mobile and changed margins exposed it.

The candidate applies current theme and typography in the synchronous render hook, expands the new view before target measurement, and gives page margins to the paginator as its gap setting. The current appearance ref also initializes the theme registry after a pending archive fetch. Existing double-display resume workarounds are removed.

An actual Gatsby cold one-click viewport proof and a long-chapter desktop/mobile regression were seen red then green. Real pointer editing preserves the native annotation identity. Changed appearance carries into a cold chapter, and live margin reflow preserves the visible passage. All six existing HTTP-to-browser resume cases pass unchanged; four failed on the intermediate manual-padding candidate. Public release and final artifact gates remain pending.

resolution.note: Resolved in candidate, not released: synchronous typography and paginator-owned margins; original-red/fixed-green cold navigation, desktop/mobile appearance, trusted editing, and six unchanged HTTP-to-browser resume cases. Final artifact and CI gates remain required.

title: Reader first navigation measures text before final page appearance
